title: The Young Man Who Gave Up Everything
script: Narrator: [warmly] Before he became a Muslim, Mus'ab ibn Umair was probably the most fashionable young man in all of Makkah.
Narrator: [thoughtful] His family was wealthy, so he always wore the finest clothes and the sweetest perfume that money could buy.
Narrator: [reflective] When he first heard the Prophet's message, he went secretly, because he was afraid of what his family would think.
Narrator: [serious] Although his mother threatened to lock him away, Mus'ab refused to abandon his new faith, no matter what she said.
Narrator: [sadly] Eventually, she stopped feeding him well and took away his comfortable clothes, hoping that hunger would change his mind.
Narrator: [with admiration] It never did. He simply accepted a harder life, since his faith mattered more to him than comfort ever had.
Narrator: [proudly] Later, the Prophet chose him for an important task, sending him to Madinah to teach the new religion there.
Narrator: [thoughtful] This was remarkable, because Mus'ab was young and had no experience teaching anyone, yet he traveled there gladly.
Narrator: [warmly] While he was in Madinah, he taught patiently, and because of his gentle manner, many families accepted Islam that year.
Narrator: [with wonder] People said that when Mus'ab spoke, even skeptical listeners softened, since his sincerity was impossible to ignore or doubt.
Narrator: [serious] Years later, at the Battle of Uhud, Mus'ab carried the Muslim flag and stood firmly beside the Prophet until the end.
Narrator: [tense] When enemies surrounded him, he kept fighting bravely, although he must have known that the danger around him was growing.
Narrator: [sadly] He was killed that day, and when his companions looked for a cloth to bury him, they found only one small piece.
Narrator: [with feeling] It was so small that if they covered his head, his feet showed, and if they covered his feet, his head showed.
Narrator: [reflective] The Prophet wept, remembering the young man who once wore the finest silk, now buried in barely any cloth at all.
Narrator: [warmly] Whenever I think of Mus'ab, I remember that true richness was never about what he owned, but about what he believed.

quiz.question: What was Mus'ab ibn Umair known for before becoming Muslim?
options: Being the most fashionable young man in Makkah
quiz.explanation: The narrator says Mus'ab was probably the most fashionable young man in all of Makkah, from a wealthy family.

quiz.question: How did Mus'ab's mother try to change his mind?
options: She stopped feeding him well and took away his comfortable clothes
quiz.explanation: She stopped feeding him well and took away his comfortable clothes, hoping hunger would change his mind.

quiz.question: What task did the Prophet give Mus'ab?
options: To go teach Islam in Madinah
quiz.explanation: The Prophet sent him to Madinah to teach the new religion there, even though he was young and inexperienced.

quiz.question: What role did Mus'ab play at the Battle of Uhud?
options: He carried the Muslim flag beside the Prophet
quiz.explanation: At the Battle of Uhud, Mus'ab carried the Muslim flag and stood firmly beside the Prophet until the end.

quiz.question: What happened when his companions tried to bury him?
options: They found only one small piece of cloth, too small to cover him fully
They could not find his body
They buried him without any ceremony
quiz.explanation: The cloth was so small that covering his head left his feet showing, and covering his feet left his head showing.

title: A Podcast on Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and the Answered Prayer
script: Host: [warmly] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Hasan, who researches the early archers of Islam. Thanks for joining me.
Guest: [pleasantly] Thank you for inviting me. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas is one of my favorite companions to talk about.
Host: [curious] I've heard he was famous for something specific. What made him stand out among the others?
Guest: [thoughtful] He was known as an incredibly skilled archer, and the Prophet once said he would sacrifice his own parents for Sa'd's sake.
Host: [surprised] That's a strong statement. Why did the Prophet say something so powerful about him?
Guest: [explaining] Because Sa'd faced enormous pressure from his mother, who refused to eat until he abandoned his new religion.
Host: [worried] That sounds like an impossible situation. What did Sa'd do when she stopped eating?
Guest: [reflective] He told her gently that although he loved her deeply, he would never leave his faith, even if she starved herself completely.
Host: [thoughtful] That must have been painful, choosing between his mother's demands and his own beliefs.
Guest: [warmly] It was, but he stayed firm, and eventually his mother ate again, since she realized nothing would change his decision.
Host: [interested] Was he also known for his prayers being answered quickly?
Guest: [nodding] Yes, exactly. The Prophet prayed that Sa'd's prayers would always be accepted, because his money and food were always earned honestly.
Host: [curious] So because his income was clean, his prayers carried special power?
Guest: [smiling] That's how many scholars explain it. Honest living was connected directly to sincere, powerful prayer in his case.
Host: [amazed] What happened to Sa'd later in his life?
Guest: [proudly] He became a respected military commander and led armies during important battles, always remembered for his courage and discipline.
Host: [smiling] Thank you, Hasan, for sharing such a moving story about loyalty and honesty today.
Guest: [warmly] Thank you for having me. I hope his example reminds someone to stay firm during difficult family pressure.

quiz.question: What was Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas especially known for?
quiz.explanation: The guest explains he was known as an incredibly skilled archer, praised directly by the Prophet.

quiz.question: What did Sa'd's mother do to pressure him?
options: She refused to eat until he left his religion
quiz.explanation: His mother refused to eat until he abandoned his new religion, hoping to force him to change.

quiz.question: How did Sa'd respond to his mother's pressure?
options: He stayed firm, saying he would never leave his faith
quiz.explanation: He told her gently that he would never leave his faith, even if she starved herself completely.

quiz.question: Why did the Prophet say Sa'd's prayers were always accepted?
options: Because his money and food were always earned honestly
Because he was the oldest companion
quiz.explanation: The Prophet connected Sa'd's accepted prayers to the fact that his money and food were always earned honestly.

quiz.question: What did Sa'd become later in his life?
quiz.explanation: He became a respected military commander, remembered for his courage and discipline in important battles.

title: Two Coworkers Discuss Umm Salamah's Long Journey
script: Dewi: [thoughtful] Fajar, I've been reading about Umm Salamah lately, and her story keeps surprising me every time I return to it.
Fajar: [curious] I don't know much about her. What makes her story so unusual compared to the others?
Dewi: [reflective] Well, when she and her husband decided to migrate to Madinah, her own family stopped them at the city gate.
Fajar: [surprised] Wait, her family physically prevented her from leaving? That seems shocking, since migration was supposed to be voluntary.
Dewi: [sadly] Exactly. They took her son away from her arms and forced her husband to travel without them, alone and worried.
Fajar: [wincing] So she was separated from her husband and her child at the same time? That sounds incredibly painful.
Dewi: [nodding] It was. She sat by that gate every single day for almost a year, crying quietly and waiting for news.
Fajar: [thoughtful] A year is a long time to wait, especially not knowing whether you would ever see your family again.
Dewi: [warmly] Eventually, her relatives felt ashamed of their cruelty, so they finally allowed her to travel and reunite with her son.
Fajar: [relieved] That must have felt like the happiest day of her entire life, after so much suffering and uncertainty.
Dewi: [smiling] It truly was. And later, after her husband passed away, she became one of the Prophet's wives, known for her sharp wisdom.
Fajar: [interested] Wisdom? Can you give me an example of that?
Dewi: [explaining] During a difficult treaty, when the men hesitated to follow an instruction, she quietly suggested a solution that solved everything calmly.
Fajar: [amazed] So her advice actually changed the outcome of an important political moment? That's impressive for anyone.
Dewi: [reflective] Exactly. Whenever I feel forgotten or unheard, I remember Umm Salamah waiting patiently by that gate for a whole year.
Fajar: [smiling] That's a powerful reminder. Patience really can lead somewhere, even after the longest and hardest waiting.

quiz.question: What happened when Umm Salamah tried to migrate to Madinah?
options: She traveled easily with her family
Her family stopped her at the city gate and took her son away
quiz.explanation: Her own family stopped them at the city gate, took her son away, and forced her husband to travel without them.

quiz.question: How long did Umm Salamah wait by the gate?
quiz.explanation: Dewi says she sat by that gate every single day for almost a year, waiting for news.

quiz.question: Why did her relatives eventually let her go?
options: They felt ashamed of their cruelty
quiz.explanation: Her relatives eventually felt ashamed of their cruelty, so they allowed her to travel and reunite with her son.

quiz.question: What was Umm Salamah known for later in her life?
quiz.explanation: After becoming one of the Prophet's wives, she became known for her sharp wisdom.

quiz.question: What does Dewi remember when she feels forgotten or unheard?
options: Umm Salamah waiting patiently by the gate for a whole year
quiz.explanation: Dewi says she remembers Umm Salamah waiting patiently by that gate for a whole year.

title: The Loyalty of Zayd ibn Harithah
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Zayd ibn Harithah's story begins with a painful loss, because he was captured and separated from his family as a child.
Narrator: [reflective] He eventually became part of the Prophet's household, and although his life had started with hardship, he was treated with genuine kindness there.
Narrator: [warmly] Years passed, and when Zayd's real father finally learned where he was living, he traveled a great distance to bring him home.
Narrator: [surprised] The father offered money for his son's freedom, expecting Zayd to run joyfully back into his arms without hesitation.
Narrator: [with wonder] But the Prophet gave Zayd an unusual choice, telling him he could freely choose to leave or freely choose to stay.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Zayd's answer shocked everyone standing there, because he chose to remain, saying he had never known kindness like this before.
Narrator: [sadly] His father was heartbroken and confused, since he could not understand why his own son would choose to stay away from him.
Narrator: [warmly] Moved by this loyalty, the Prophet publicly adopted Zayd, and for years afterward, people called him Zayd, son of Muhammad.
Narrator: [reflective] This decision showed how deeply Zayd trusted the man who had treated him with dignity when almost no one else had.
Narrator: [serious] Later, Zayd became a trusted leader, and the Prophet placed him in command of important missions and military expeditions.
Narrator: [with admiration] Although some questioned why a formerly enslaved man led respected soldiers, the Prophet trusted his judgment completely, without hesitation or doubt.
Narrator: [sadly] Zayd was eventually killed in battle while leading his troops bravely, refusing to retreat even as the danger grew severe.
Narrator: [reflective] When news of his death reached the Prophet, he wept, since Zayd had been like a true son to him for many years.
Narrator: [warmly] Whenever people ask me about loyalty, I think of Zayd choosing kindness over blood, and trust over an easier, more familiar path.
Narrator: [peacefully] His story reminds me that family isn't only about where we come from, but also about where we finally feel safe and valued.

quiz.question: How did Zayd ibn Harithah's story begin?
options: He was captured and separated from his family as a child
He was a soldier from birth
quiz.explanation: Zayd was captured and separated from his family as a child before joining the Prophet's household.

quiz.question: What choice did the Prophet give Zayd when his father arrived?
options: To freely choose to leave with his father or freely choose to stay
To leave without speaking to anyone
quiz.explanation: The Prophet gave Zayd an unusual choice, telling him he could freely choose to leave or freely choose to stay.

quiz.question: What did Zayd choose, and why did it shock people?
options: He chose to leave with his father
He chose to stay, saying he had never known kindness like this before
He asked to be sold again
quiz.explanation: Zayd chose to remain, shocking everyone by saying he had never known kindness like this before.

quiz.question: What did the Prophet do after Zayd's decision?
quiz.explanation: Moved by this loyalty, the Prophet publicly adopted Zayd, and people called him Zayd, son of Muhammad.

quiz.question: How did Zayd die?
options: In battle, leading his troops bravely without retreating
quiz.explanation: Zayd was eventually killed in battle while leading his troops bravely, refusing to retreat even as danger grew severe.

title: A Phone Call About Fatimah's Quiet Strength
script: Amir: [thoughtful] Mom, I read something today about Fatimah, the Prophet's youngest daughter, and I wanted to ask you about it.
Mother: [warmly] Of course. Fatimah's life is one I've loved learning about since I was young myself.
Amir: [curious] The article said her family lived very simply, even though her father was the Prophet. Is that accurate?
Mother: [nodding] Completely accurate. Sometimes their home had almost no food, and Fatimah worked constantly, grinding grain until her hands ached badly.
Amir: [surprised] That sounds exhausting. Didn't she ever ask her father for an easier life, considering who he was?
Mother: [gently] She did ask once, actually. She wanted a servant to help with the heavy, endless housework she faced every single day.
Amir: [curious] What did the Prophet say when she asked him for help?
Mother: [reflective] Instead of giving her a servant, he taught her special words to say before sleeping, promising they would bring lasting strength.
Amir: [thoughtful] So he offered comfort for her heart, rather than simply removing her difficult physical work?
Mother: [warmly] Exactly, and Fatimah accepted this answer without complaint, because she trusted her father's wisdom completely, even when it surprised her.
Amir: [interested] Was she close to her father in other ways too?
Mother: [smiling] Very close. Whenever he traveled and returned home, she was often the first person he visited, before anyone else.
Amir: [curious] That's touching. Did she stay strong even after he passed away?
Mother: [sadly] She grieved deeply, since losing him affected her more than almost anyone else in the entire community.
Amir: [reflective] It sounds like her strength wasn't about having an easy life, but about carrying hardship with real grace and quiet dignity.
Mother: [warmly] Exactly, my son. That's why so many people still admire her, even so many centuries later.

quiz.question: How did Fatimah's family live, according to the mother?
options: Very simply, sometimes with almost no food
quiz.explanation: The mother says their home had almost no food, and Fatimah worked constantly grinding grain.

quiz.question: What did Fatimah once ask her father for?
options: A servant to help with heavy housework
quiz.explanation: She asked for a servant to help with the heavy, endless housework she faced every day.

quiz.question: How did the Prophet respond to her request?
options: He gave her a servant immediately
He taught her special words to say before sleeping for strength
quiz.explanation: Instead of giving her a servant, he taught her special words to say before sleeping, promising lasting strength.

quiz.question: How did Fatimah react to her father's answer?
options: She accepted it without complaint, trusting his wisdom
She refused to speak to him
She asked someone else for help
quiz.explanation: Fatimah accepted this answer without complaint, because she trusted her father's wisdom completely.

quiz.question: What is the mother's main point about Fatimah's strength?
options: It came from having an easy life
It came from carrying hardship with grace and quiet dignity
It came from avoiding all difficulty
quiz.explanation: The mother concludes that Fatimah's strength was about carrying hardship with real grace and quiet dignity.

title: Understanding Abu Ubaidah, the Trusted One
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When people list qualities they admire most in a leader, they often mention courage or intelligence, but rarely mention plain trustworthiness.
Narrator: [reflective] That's exactly why I find Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah so interesting, since trust was the very center of his entire reputation.
Narrator: [warmly] The Prophet once described him as the trusted guardian of this whole community, a title given to no other companion.
Narrator: [serious] Once, when the Prophet needed someone reliable to lead a group into Yemen, he chose Abu Ubaidah without a moment of doubt.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Before they left, he asked the Prophet for guidance about handling difficult situations that might arise during such a long journey.
Narrator: [calm] The Prophet answered simply, telling him to remain honest in everything, because honesty would protect him more than any weapon could.
Narrator: [warmly] Abu Ubaidah carried that lesson everywhere, and although he later led armies and controlled vast wealth, he lived extremely modestly himself.
Narrator: [with admiration] Soldiers said he shared their simple food and slept among them, refusing any special comfort just because of his rank.
Narrator: [reflective] Once, during a difficult military campaign, food became scarce, and everyone, including Abu Ubaidah, survived mainly on leaves from nearby trees.
Narrator: [thoughtful] Despite that hardship, he never complained publicly, since he believed that leaders should endure difficulty before asking others to endure it.
Narrator: [warmly] When Umar later became caliph, he trusted Abu Ubaidah completely, sending him to manage some of the most sensitive regional affairs.
Narrator: [sadly] Sadly, Abu Ubaidah eventually died during a serious illness that spread through the region he was governing at the time.
Narrator: [reflective] Even as he was dying, he reportedly gave calm, practical advice to those gathered around him, thinking of the community until the end.
Narrator: [warmly] What stays with me about Abu Ubaidah isn't power or fame, but the quiet consistency of a man who never once betrayed the trust placed in him.

quiz.question: What title did the Prophet give Abu Ubaidah?
options: The trusted guardian of this community
quiz.explanation: The Prophet described him as the trusted guardian of this whole community, a title given to no other companion.

quiz.question: What advice did the Prophet give him before the journey to Yemen?
options: To collect as much wealth as possible
To remain honest in everything, since honesty protects more than a weapon
quiz.explanation: The Prophet told him to remain honest in everything, because honesty would protect him more than any weapon could.

quiz.question: How did Abu Ubaidah live despite leading armies and controlling wealth?
options: Extremely modestly, sharing simple food with soldiers
quiz.explanation: Soldiers said he shared their simple food and slept among them, refusing special comfort because of his rank.

quiz.question: What happened during the difficult military campaign mentioned in the story?
options: Food became scarce, and they survived mainly on leaves
quiz.explanation: Food became scarce during the campaign, and everyone, including Abu Ubaidah, survived mainly on leaves from nearby trees.

quiz.question: How did Abu Ubaidah die?
options: During a serious illness that spread through the region he governed
Peacefully at an old age at home
quiz.explanation: Abu Ubaidah eventually died during a serious illness that spread through the region he was governing.

title: A Radio Segment on Abu Hurairah's Devotion to Learning
script: Radio Host: [cheerfully] Good morning, listeners! Today we're discussing Abu Hurairah, a companion famous for remembering countless sayings of the Prophet. We have a caller. Hello!
Caller: [a little nervous] Hello! Thank you for taking my call this morning. I've admired this companion for years.
Radio Host: [warmly] Wonderful! Can you tell us what made his situation so different from many other companions?
Caller: [thoughtful] Yes, gladly. Unlike some companions, Abu Hurairah was extremely poor and often had nothing but a small piece of bread each day.
Radio Host: [curious] So how did someone so poor become known for remembering so much knowledge?
Caller: [reflective] Because he dedicated almost all his time to staying near the Prophet, listening carefully whenever there was something to learn.
Radio Host: [interested] Didn't he need to work, though, to survive financially like everyone else?
Caller: [explaining] He did work sometimes, but he chose to prioritize learning over earning more money, even though hunger frequently affected him.
Radio Host: [surprised] That's a difficult choice. Wasn't he ever tempted to focus on his own comfort instead?
Caller: [warmly] Certainly, but he once said that other companions were busy trading in markets, while he stayed close, learning quietly and patiently.
Radio Host: [amazed] So while others built wealth, he built knowledge instead. That's a remarkable difference in priorities.
Caller: [nodding] Exactly, and because of that daily closeness, he later reported thousands of sayings, more than almost any other companion.
Radio Host: [curious] Did people trust everything he reported, considering how much he shared?
Caller: [honestly] Most scholars trusted him deeply, although some questioned him at first, since remembering so much seemed almost impossible to believe.
Radio Host: [interested] How did he respond to that doubt from other people?
Caller: [smiling] He explained that other companions were often occupied with trade, while his empty stomach kept him sitting close, absorbing every single lesson.
Radio Host: [warmly] What an incredible example of turning hardship into something so valuable for future generations to benefit from.
Caller: [sincerely] Thank you for listening. I hope his dedication encourages someone today whose circumstances feel limiting right now.

quiz.question: What made Abu Hurairah's situation different from many other companions?
options: He was extremely poor and often had little food
quiz.explanation: The caller explains that Abu Hurairah was extremely poor and often had nothing but a small piece of bread each day.

quiz.question: Why did Abu Hurairah remember so many sayings of the Prophet?
options: He dedicated almost all his time to staying near the Prophet, listening carefully
He was taught by his family
He heard them from other companions only
quiz.explanation: He dedicated almost all his time to staying near the Prophet, listening carefully whenever there was something to learn.

quiz.question: What choice did Abu Hurairah make regarding work and learning?
options: He prioritized learning over earning more money, even facing hunger
quiz.explanation: He chose to prioritize learning over earning more money, even though hunger frequently affected him.

quiz.question: How many sayings did Abu Hurairah later report?
options: Thousands, more than almost any other companion
quiz.explanation: Because of his daily closeness to the Prophet, he later reported thousands of sayings, more than almost any other companion.

quiz.question: Why did some people question Abu Hurairah at first?
options: Remembering so much seemed almost impossible to believe
quiz.explanation: Some questioned him at first, since remembering so much seemed almost impossible to believe, though most scholars trusted him deeply.
